title: The Unofficial Group Chat
premise: Oscar Zhou, a scholarship student at Ashford Academy, has survived four years by being exactly what the school needs: quiet, grateful, invisible. When an anonymous group chat starts circulating answers to a college essay prompt — 'What truth have you never said aloud?' — the confessions that flood in expose everything from petty cruelties to the fact that the academy's beloved founder's fortune was built on stolen land, land Oscar's grandmother once owned. As the chat spirals and the administration hunts its creator, Oscar realizes he knows who made it: Juniper Hale, the headmaster's daughter, who built it to force her own confession into the open. Together they must decide whether to hand the evidence of the land theft to the press before graduation — knowing it will burn down the school funding both their futures. In the end, Oscar publishes the truth under his own name, loses his scholarship, and gains something better: a community, a cause, and Juniper, choosing him over duty.
about_author: Marguerite Eastwick is the pen name of a former boarding school teacher who spent a decade watching teenagers say true things in group chats they'd never say aloud. She writes from a small coastal town where she keeps a suspicious number of houseplants.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet Oscar mid-performance: tutoring rich kids, editing his essay for the tenth time, dodging questions about his family. A scholarship audit letter arrives, reminding him how conditional his place is. Emotional beat: the exhausting tightrope of gratitude, establishing what he stands to lose.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. English class assigns the honest-question essay; that night, an anonymous group chat appears in every senior's phone, inviting real answers. The first confessions are funny, then not. Oscar watches, refusing to type. Emotional beat: voyeuristic thrill curdling into dread as he recognizes names in the confessions.

chapters.title: Juniper Hale
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Inside the chat's creator: the headmaster's daughter, brilliant and suffocating, who started it as a controlled detonation for one confession of her own. She notices Oscar is the only one not posting — and finds that interesting. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as power.

chapters.title: The Land
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A confession about the founder's 'gifted' estate sends Oscar to his grandmother's boxes, where he finds deeds proving the Zhou family land was taken in 1962 to build the academy. His scholarship suddenly looks like hush money. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — not money, but a debt owed to him.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The administration traces devices; students are interrogated in pairs. Oscar and Juniper are caught together and forced to share a detention, where each realizes the other knows more than they're saying. Emotional beat: two careful people recognizing a fellow liar — with reluctant delight.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper shows Oscar the chat's backend and confesses her own truth: she reported her brother's assault by a donor's son, and her father buried it. The chat was meant to force it back into daylight. Emotional beat: love beginning as conspiracy, trust extended like a held breath.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The headmaster offers Oscar a full-ride plus a named scholarship if he helps identify the chat's creator — while Juniper's father quietly threatens her mother's custody arrangement. Both are bought with their families' futures. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose; Oscar almost says yes.

chapters.title: What Truth Have You Never Said Aloud
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar writes the essay he's been avoiding — about the land, the silence, the price of gratitude — and instead of submitting it to colleges, drafts it for the chat. Juniper begs him not to, terrified of what it costs him. Emotional beat: the quiet moment of decision, choosing self over safety.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. At commencement, before donors and cameras, Oscar takes the mic during the founder tribute and reads his essay aloud; simultaneously, Juniper releases the chat archive and her brother's case file to the press. Chaos, applause, fury. Emotional beat: terror transfiguring into clarity — justice done loudly, outside the law.

chapters.title: The Unofficial Group Chat
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, months later. The academy faces investigation; Oscar lost the scholarship but won a journalism mentorship funded by alumni who read the chat. Juniper visits with news her brother's case reopened. The final scene: a new group chat, just the two of them, answering the prompt honestly at last. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed — a future built on truth instead of silence.
